newsitem.title: USA: Hoechst plans 2 Singapore acetyl plants.
newsitem.headline: Hoechst plans 2 Singapore acetyl plants.

text.p: Hoechst AG's Hoechst Global Basic Chemicals said Wednesday it plans to build two grass-roots acetyl plants in Singapore.
It said a 500,000 ton acetic acid unit will begin production no later than January 2001 and a 100,000 ton acetate ester unit will be onstream in 1999's fourth quarter.
The company said these investments were approved by the Hoechst AG board on May 20, but it declined to give the expected cost of the units to be built on Sakra Island.
Hoechst noted it will start up a 170,000 ton per year vinyl acetate monomer unit on Sakra Island in July.

Hoechst said it will employ its acid-optimization technology for the acetic acid unit, which will provide feedstock for both the acetate monomer and acetate ester units. The acetate ester unit will produce butyl and ethyl acetate and have the capability of making other esters.
Hoechst Global also pointed out that, as announced in Hoechst's annual report, it will be named Celanese as of July 1, taking on the name of the U.S. chemical company Hoechst acquired 10 years ago.
